jsonld.headline: One-Pan Tuscan Chicken

publisher.name: The Kitchn
publisher.ownershipFundingInfo: The Kitchn is privately owned by Maxwell Ryan and funded through revenue generated by advertising sales, affiliate commissions, and licensing.

jsonld.description: This tender chicken cooked in a creamy sauce with sun-dried tomatoes and spinach is totally irresistible.
recipeIngredient: 2  large boneless, skinless chicken breasts (1 1/2 to 2 pounds total)
1/2 cup drained oil-packed sun-dried tomatoes (2 1/2 ounces), thinly sliced
1 ounce Parmesan cheese (1/2 cup firmly packed freshly grated or 1/3 cup store-bought grated)

recipeInstructions.name: Step 1
recipeInstructions.text: Cut 2 large boneless, skinless chicken breasts in half horizontally (also known as butterflying). Pat dry with paper towels. Season all over with 1 teaspoon of the kosher salt and 1/2 teaspoon black pepper.

recipeInstructions.name: Step 2
recipeInstructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add half of the chicken in a single layer and sear until browned, 3 to 5 minutes per side. Transfer to a large plate (the chicken will not be cooked through). Add 1 tablespoon of the olive oil to the pan and repeat browning the remaining chicken. Transfer to the same plate.

recipeInstructions.name: Step 3
recipeInstructions.text: Reduce the heat to medium. Add the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil, if needed, and heat until shimmering. Add 1 diced small yellow onion and cook, stirring occasionally until softened, 2 to 3 minutes. Add 3 minced garlic cloves, 1/2 cup thinly sliced sun-dried tomatoes, and 2 teaspoons dried Italian seasoning. Cook until fragrant, 30 seconds to 1 minute. Add 5 ounces baby spinach a handful at a time. Cook, stirring regularly, until just wilted, 1 to 2 minutes.

recipeInstructions.name: Step 4
recipeInstructions.text: Add 1 ounce grated Parmesan cheese, 1 1/4 cups heavy cream, and the remaining 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt. Bring to a simmer, scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the pan with a wooden spoon. Reduce the heat to maintain a gentle simmer. Return the chicken and any accumulated juices on the plate to the pan and cook until the chicken is cooked through and registers at least 165ºF on an instant-read thermometer, 4 to 7 minutes.

itemListElement.text: Storage: Refrigerate leftovers in an airtight container for up to 4 days.

review.reviewBody: This dish came out perfect! My wife thinks that thighs would work better but I loved the flavor
I made it for two, and we both loved it.  It was really easy to make!
Great easy recipe!   I didn't have the tomatoes so I used a small can of tomato paste.    Really good.  Will definitely make it again.
One of the best at home chicken recipes I've found!

I happen to live in America! I love authentic food when I would visit that country. However, I don’t appreciate the negative comments. Different tastes for different folks. I have friends different countries, they invite me to a cook out. They make an American dish, no it’s not what I would make it has their own spin on it. I appreciate that. No need to call them out, IDC what they call it. If it’s good! Call it a recipe 🥰 You can name it what ever the heck you want🥰
Added a glass of medium Sherry after the sunny Tom's went in and reduced before adding the cream. Severed with pasta and ate with a teary eye🥲

Excellent and elegant recipe. I had diced chicken and angel hair on hand so I used that, but I'd like to try it over whipped potatoes next time. Easily adaptable to suit your household's tastes. My kids won't go near an onion so I left that out and it was delicious anyway. Everyone had seconds.

This may not be eaten in Tuscany but it is definitely one of the best chicken dishes  I’ve made .   Full of flavor and oh so delicious and comforting.  Easy to put together.   Made 1/2 recipe to try it out before making it for company.  I substituted thighs for breasts - wonderful.   We used fresh Italian bread for sopping up sauce.   Will consider doubling sauce and possibly serving over pasta.Can this dish be prepared early in afternoon, refrigerated before cooking thru chicken, then reheated and served.

This is such a delicious chicken recipe. Definitely a permanent meal in my house. It is super easy to make. The aromas that fill the house will surely get your appetite going. I've made it with light meat and dark meat, sun dried tomatoes and regular tomatoes. And it is always delicious. The only downside is there won't be much leftovers.

It was fine, but we didn't think it lived up to the hype.  The sauce felt a little flat, like it needed a splash of acid. If I make this again, I'll add either some white wine, or squeeze of lemon to bring a little depth.

My friend was visiting and made this recipe for a dinner gathering last night.  It was absolutely delicious. I'm so happy there are leftovers.  My friend added mushrooms which was a nice addition.  She served this with orzo which was a great compliment.  With the yummy veggies in the recipe, we skipped a salad and served broiled parmesan asparagus.  We all felt we were eating a fine Italian bistro.

reviewedBy.description: Tara Holland is a British mom of two teenage girls residing in Brooklyn. She changed her successful career midlife from the financial corporate world to follow her culinary dream and graduated with honors at the Institute of Culinary Education in 2017. She went on to become an Assistant Food Editor at Rachael Ray Every Day magazine, and is now a freelance recipe developer, writer, and recipe tester.

jsonld.abstract: Why You’ll Love My Tuscan Chicken It’s top-rated! My Tuscan chicken recipe has earned rave reviews thanks to its rich, comforting flavors and creamy sauce. Big flavor payoff. I pack every bite with juicy chicken, sun-dried tomatoes, and Parmesan for a dinner that never disappoints.
